customers.evidence: We believe our first responsibility is to the doctors, nurses and patients, to mothers and fathers and all others who use our products and services.

employees.evidence: We are responsible to our employees, the men and women who work with us throughout the world.

dei.evidence: There must be equal opportunity for employment, development and advancement for those qualified.

environment.evidence: We must maintain in good order the property we are privileged to use, protecting the environment and natural resources.

community.evidence: We must be good citizens – support good works and charities and bear our fair share of taxes.

shareholders.evidence: Our final responsibility is to our stockholders.

integrity.evidence: We must provide competent management, and their actions must be just and ethical.

safety.evidence: Compensation must be fair and adequate, and working conditions clean, orderly and safe.

innovation.evidence: We must experiment with new ideas. Research must be carried on, innovative programs developed and mistakes paid for.

result.analyst_notes: Aspirational, credo-based framing using first-person plural and directive must language throughout. Stakeholders are addressed in a fixed sequence: customers, employees, community, then stockholders last. Commitments are stated absolutely, with little hedging. The page cites the 1943 founding of the Credo and frames it as a business-success recipe.
